eventMetadata.context_description: **Current forecast consensus from models and regional observations supports a daily maximum near 32°C for Panama City on August 9, 2026, during the peak of the wet season.** Typical August conditions feature high humidity, frequent afternoon thunderstorms driven by daytime heating and sea-breeze convergence, and average highs of 29–31°C that rarely exceed 32–33°C without unusual clearing. Traders have priced 32°C at 97.5% because deviations would require atypical atmospheric stability or reduced moisture, both uncommon in climatological records for early August. A shift to clearer skies or a drier air mass could push readings to 33–34°C, while stronger convection might hold the peak at or below 31°C.

Climatologically, August highs average 25–29°C, but the current subsidence pattern has sustained above-average temperatures without frontal passages or significant convective cooling.

Recent model runs show tight clustering around 32°C as the most probable peak, aligning with the market’s 59.5% implied probability for that outcome and 31.5% for 31°C. Minor upside risk to 33°C exists if boundary-layer mixing is delayed or local stations record slightly higher values, while downside scenarios would require unexpected marine air intrusion or rapid cloud buildup—developments not supported by the latest consensus. Traders are weighting the stable synoptic setup and limited forecast spread, with resolution hinging on the official 24-hour maximum reported for Paris.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the King Abdulaziz International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 10 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the King Abdulaziz International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/sa/jeddah/OEJN.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Latest forecast models for Jeddah on August 10 indicate a hot day with daytime highs near or slightly above seasonal norms in its hot desert climate, moderated by Red Sea humidity and sea breezes, positioning 40–41°C ranges as the leading market-implied outcomes.** 

Official outlooks from Saudi Arabia’s National Center for Meteorology note August temperatures up to 2.5°C above normal across the Makkah region, consistent with typical August averages of 37–38°C highs that can push higher under clear, sunny conditions with light northwesterly winds. BBC and other models currently project around 39°C, while broader seasonal guidance and recent model consensus support trader pricing that favors a modest chance of reaching or exceeding 40–41°C. Resolution hinges on the official peak reading amid low precipitation risk and stable atmospheric patterns.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Recent ensemble forecasts from Météo-France and ECMWF place the August 11 maximum temperature in Paris near 31–32 °C under a transient high-pressure ridge delivering mostly sunny skies and light winds.** Daytime heating is favored by clear conditions and minimal cloud cover, while gentle northerly or northwesterly flow limits advection of warmer air. Historical August climatology shows typical highs of 24–29 °C, so current guidance reflects above-average but not extreme warmth. Minor differences among model runs—arising from subtle variations in boundary-layer mixing, exact timing of any thin high cloud, or small shifts in the ridge axis—create the narrow spread that keeps 30–32 °C outcomes closely matched in trader probabilities. Updated model cycles and Météo-France briefings over the next 48 hours remain the key catalysts that could refine these odds.

Ensemble model consensus supports daytime highs near 34–36°C under typical August humidity and light winds, consistent with historical climatology of 32–34°C averages but elevated by recent subsidence. Market-implied odds cluster on 35°C as the modal outcome because updated guidance shows modest warming potential without full tropical moisture return, while spread across adjacent bins reflects residual uncertainty in exact timing of stabilization and any lingering showers. New CWA briefings ahead of peak heating will likely refine these probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model guidance and climatological patterns for Chongqing’s subtropical summer position the 36°C outcome as the narrow market leader at 35.5% implied probability, followed closely by 37°C. Persistent high-pressure ridging, regional monsoon moisture, and the city’s urban heat-island effect typically produce daily maxima near the long-term August average of 34–35°C, yet occasional short-wave ridging can add 1–3°C on any given day. Forecasters note modest day-to-day variability from steering flows and localized convection that can either suppress or enhance peak readings by a degree or two. With resolution two days away, updated high-resolution runs from agencies such as the China Meteorological Administration will likely tighten the range among the tightly bunched 35–37°C brackets.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Monsoon-driven cloud cover and scattered rainfall are the dominant factors capping Lucknow's August 11 maximum near 33–34 °C.** In the peak of the southwest monsoon, frequent cloud decks reduce incoming solar radiation while evaporative cooling from light precipitation and high humidity (typically 75–85 %) limits daytime heating, keeping maxima close to the long-term August average of ~32–33 °C. Recent India Meteorological Department guidance and multi-model consensus (GFS/ECMWF) point to partly cloudy skies with isolated showers on the 11th, conditions that have produced 33 °C readings on the preceding days and align with the market’s heaviest volume on the 33 °C and 34 °C bins (28.5 % and 40.5 %).  

Slight model spread in timing and intensity of any showers creates the modest probability mass on 35 °C (15 %), while the low odds on extremes reflect the low historical frequency of sub-32 °C or 36 °C+ days under active monsoon flow this late in the season. Updated IMD bulletins and next model runs within 24–48 hours will be the key data releases that could shift these implied probabilities.
